text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-Prime Minister Hariri reaches agreement with Maronite Patriarch Sfeir about the issue of the religious audiovisual media. Under the deal, the religious authorities will supervise and prepare the programmes and the government will broadcast them.
-U.S. ambassador to Lebanon Jones says freedom of expression is an important Lebanese tradition and liberating Lebanon can be achieved by having strong armed forces.
-Greenpeace ship barred from entering Beirut port stops at the edge of Lebanese territorial waters and will wait for official permission to enter until noon today.

-Minister of Interior Murr attacks the constitutional council says his ministry is not employed by it after the high court openly criticised the ministry for delaying the delivery of documents needed to discuss appeals from defeated candidates in the last parliamentary elections.
-Minister of displaced people Jumblatt says he is not ready to "sink with the government's ship".
-Syrian Defence Minister Lieutenant-General Tlas has visited Syrian forces in Lebanon.
